steps.instruction: Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in the browser, sign in to Grafana with username 'admin' and password 'admin' (if a password-change prompt appears, skip it). Then find and open the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (use search/dashboards if needed) and report the titles of all panels on that dashboard, exactly as shown on the page, as a list.

The Grafana save-dashboard drawer is currently open in the browser at http://127.0.0.1:3000/. There is a textbox labeled 'Save dashboard title field' currently containing 'New dashboard', and a 'Save' button in the drawer. Do exactly two things, one at a time, NOT as a batch: first clear the textbox and type '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' into it; then click the Save button. After that, report the browser's current URL and whether the dashboard saved successfully.

In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-open.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard, add a new Text panel to the dashboard. Set the panel title to exactly '{{runid}} Notes' and set the text content to include the runid, e.g. 'Bench run {{runid}} — notes panel'. Then save the dashboard (Ctrl+S opens the save drawer; click Save). Verify the save succeeded (no unsaved-changes indicator, 'Discard panel changes' disabled) and report the panel title and text content as shown on the dashboard.

In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-open.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard, do two things and save: (1) Add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard — open the dashboard settings (gear icon), go to the General settings section, find the Tags field, add the tag 'bench'. (2) Set the dashboard's time range to the last 6 hours — open the time range picker in the top right and choose 'Last 6 hours'. Then save the dashboard (Ctrl+S then Save, or Save from settings). Verify the save succeeded and report the tags shown in dashboard settings and the time range shown in the top-right picker.

In Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-open.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard, set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m': open the time range picker (top right), find the 'Auto refresh' / refresh interval dropdown, and select '1m'. Then save the dashboard (Ctrl+S then Save). After saving, verify by reloading the dashboard page fresh at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-open.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard (no URL query params) and report: (a) the refresh interval shown in the top-right picker, (b) the time range shown in the top-right picker, (c) whether the dashboard shows any unsaved-changes indicator.

Verification task on Grafana at http://127.0.0.1:3000/. Load the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-open.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard fresh (no query params) and report these specific facts: (1) the dashboard title shown in the page header/breadcrumb; (2) the titles of every panel on the dashboard; (3) open the panel editor for the panel titled '{{runid}} Availability' and report its visualization type and which data source its query uses (then exit the editor without changing anything); (4) the text content rendered inside the panel titled '{{runid}} Notes'; (5) open dashboard Settings > General and report the tags listed; (6) the time range and refresh interval shown in the top-right picker. Do not modify anything.

Load http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-open.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard fresh in Grafana and confirm the dashboard is in a clean saved state: report whether any unsaved-changes indicator or 'Discard' button is present, the dashboard title, the panel titles, the time range, and the refresh interval. Do not click anything that would modify the dashboard.
